payload.title: Period keys in the list's time zone; what was not sent carries forward
payload.description:
The once-only key of a periodic Announcement uses the list's local date: `roundup:<list>:<yyyy-ww>` for weekly, `roundup:<list>:<yyyy-mm-dd>` for daily, from the scheduled local time and not from UTC or from when the run happened. An item is eligible for a list's next issue if it qualified since the list's last sent Delivery, not 'this calendar period'. So a week that was never released is not lost: when the next period's Announcement is created, the unreleased one is cancelled with the reason 'not released before the next period; items carried forward' and its items are eligible again.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A send delayed past midnight still belongs to its scheduled period.
- A skipped period's items appear in the next issue.
- Two ticks for one period make one Announcement.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- period-keys.feature: a late run keeps its period key; a clock change does not make two issues or none; an unreleased weekly issue is cancelled when the next begins and its items carry forward.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Newsletters and subscriptions: weekly, daily and every new item. Slice code N3 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
